intro: Unit II of the TNPSC Group 2/2A Prelims English syllabus focuses on advanced vocabulary, grammar, and word formation. Mastering these topics is essential to secure high marks in the objective-type preliminary examination.

sections.heading: Word Relationships and Usage
points: Synonyms and Antonyms: Understand contextual meanings to identify the exact opposite or similar word in a sentence.
Homonyms and Homophones: Differentiate between words that sound alike (homophones) and words that are spelled alike (homonyms).
Collocations: Learn common word pairings, such as 'heavy rain' and 'strong coffee', to ensure natural phrasing.

sections.heading: Idioms, Phrasal Verbs, and Figures of Speech
points: Idioms and Phrases: Memorize common expressions like 'break the ice' or 'piece of cake' and their contextual meanings.
Phrasal Verbs: Understand the meaning of verbs combined with prepositions or adverbs, such as 'look after' or 'give up'.
Figures of Speech: Identify metaphors, similes, personification, and hyperbole in given passages.

sections.heading: Word Formation and Singular/Plural
points: One-word Substitution: Replace long phrases with a single precise word (e.g., 'one who eats human flesh' is 'cannibal').
Derivatives: Recognize how prefixes and suffixes change the root word's meaning and part of speech.
Singular and Plural: Master regular pluralization and irregular plurals, including zero plurals (e.g., 'sheep', 'deer').

sections.heading: Abbreviations, Spelling, and English Variants
points: Abbreviations: Learn standard abbreviations for common organizations, titles, and units of measurement.
Spelling: Pay close attention to commonly misspelled words, particularly those with double letters.
British vs. American English: Be aware of spelling differences, such as 'colour' (UK) vs. 'color' (US).

exam_tips: Practice previous year TNPSC Group 2/2A question papers to understand the exact pattern of vocabulary questions.
When solving antonyms or synonyms, always read the entire sentence to grasp the exact context before selecting an answer.
Create a personal vocabulary notebook for phrasal verbs and idioms, noting their meanings and example sentences.
title: Unit II: Vocabulary
